title: WingsCrew Peanut Butter Banana Oat Bake
notes: Our take: peanut butter swirl instead of walnuts, honey instead of brown sugar, more cinnamon, no nutmeg and less salt.

ingredients.item: ripe bananas, mashed (spotty ones are best)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Butter a 9×9 dish.
Mash the bananas in a big bowl. Whisk in the eggs, honey, cinnamon, salt, vanilla and baking powder.
Stir in the milk, then the oats. Pour into the dish.
Warm the peanut butter 15 seconds in the microwave, drizzle it over the top and swirl with a knife.
Bake 40-45 minutes, until the center is set and no longer jiggles.
Cut into squares. Keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, honey, vanilla and a light pinch of salt
tryThis: a dusting of cinnamon over the peanut butter swirl
a few chocolate chips on top
seasoning.tip: Ripe, spotty bananas do most of the sweetening; greener ones need a little more honey.

title: WingsCrew PB&J Overnight Oats
notes: Our take: peanut butter and honey instead of brown sugar and chia, Welch's grape jelly swirl, half a banana instead of walnuts. 5 minutes hands-on; total includes about 8 hours chilling.
steps: In a jar, stir the peanut butter and honey into a splash of the milk until smooth.
Add the rest of the milk, the oats, cinnamon and salt. Lid on and shake.
Fridge at least 4 hours, best overnight.
Top with banana and a spoon of Welch's grape jelly. Keeps 4 days.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, honey and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a drizzle of chocolate syrup instead of the jelly
seasoning.tip: Loosen the peanut butter with a little milk first or it stays in a lump.

title: WingsCrew Ranchero Beans & Eggs
notes: Our take: Ro-Tel instead of jalapeño and water, corn oil, sharp cheddar instead of cotija, and warm corn tortillas instead of rice.

ingredients.item: black beans, 15 oz (H-E-B), 1 drained and 1 undrained
diced tomatoes & green chiles, 10 oz (H-E-B Ro-Tel style)

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet on medium. Cook the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the beans, Ro-Tel with its juice, cumin and chili powder. Simmer 5 minutes and mash some beans.
Make 4 wells and crack in the eggs. Sprinkle with Nature's Seasoning.
Lid on, medium-low, 7-10 minutes until the whites are set (longer for firm yolks).
Top with cheddar, cover 1 minute to melt, and scoop into warm corn tortillas.

seasoning.base: garlic, cumin, chili powder and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Ro-Tel and Nature's Seasoning are both salty; taste before adding any salt.

title: WingsCrew Bacon Skillet Potatoes
notes: Our take: cheap russets cooked in bacon fat with the bacon crumbled in, microwave head start instead of boiling, and Nature's Seasoning plus fresh garlic.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, skin on, ½-inch dice

steps: Microwave the diced potatoes with the water in a covered bowl 5 minutes. Drain.
Cook the bacon in a big skillet until crisp. Set it aside; leave about 2 Tbsp fat in the pan.
Spread the potatoes in one layer on medium-high and leave them 5 minutes to brown. Flip.
Add the onion and cook 6-8 minutes, until brown and tender.
Stir in the garlic, Nature's Seasoning and pepper for 1 minute. Crumble in the bacon, add the butter and serve.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic and black pepper
tryThis: shredded sharp cheddar melted on top
seasoning.tip: Bacon and Nature's Seasoning bring the salt; don't add more until you taste.

title: WingsCrew One-Pot Lentil Chili Stew
notes: Our take: one pot with no pre-soak, carrots instead of celery, Ro-Tel plus store-brand diced tomatoes, more chili powder and cumin, no turmeric or cilantro, optional sharp cheddar on top.

ingredients.item: hot sauce, to taste (Hill Country Fare Louisiana)

steps: Heat the oil in a big pot on medium. Cook the onion and carrots 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, both cans with juice, broth and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils fall apart and it's thick.
Squeeze in the lime, add salt and hot sauce to taste. Top with cheddar if you like.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin and garlic, finished with lime
seasoning.tip: Stir the bottom every few minutes; red lentils stick as they thicken.

title: WingsCrew Fajita Veggie Lentil Rice Skillet
notes: Our take: a bag of frozen fajita veggies instead of onion and corn, Ro-Tel instead of fire-roasted tomatoes, Nature's Seasoning instead of adobo and salt, and double the sharp cheddar melted on under the lid.

ingredients.item: black beans, drained and rinsed (15 oz)

steps: Cook the frozen veggies in the oil on medium-high 4-5 minutes, until the water cooks off.
Stir in the garlic and all the spices for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, beans, Ro-Tel with juice, broth and water. Boil, then cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice. Cover, bring back to a boil, then simmer on low 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat, scatter on the cheddar, lid on 5 minutes to melt.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Ro-Tel and Nature's Seasoning bring the salt; taste before adding more.

title: WingsCrew Salsa Rice & Pinto Bean Bowls
notes: Our take: cheaper pinto beans instead of black beans, rice toasted in corn oil and cooked with salsa, garlic and chili powder in the beans, and sharp cheddar.
steps: Toast the rice in the oil 2 minutes. Add the water, ½ cup salsa and the salt.
Boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Meanwhile simmer the beans with garlic, cumin and chili powder 5 minutes; mash a few.
Build bowls: rice, beans, more salsa, cheddar, green onion and sour cream.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic and salsa
seasoning.tip: Taste the beans before salting; canned beans and salsa vary a lot.

title: WingsCrew Ham & Egg Fried Rice
notes: Our take: diced ham for protein, a bag of frozen peas and carrots instead of chopping, garlic instead of fresh ginger, corn oil and a pat of butter instead of sesame oil.

ingredients.item: green onions, whites and greens split

steps: Scramble the eggs in 1 Tbsp oil until set. Move to a plate.
Add 1 Tbsp oil, the ham and frozen veggies. Cook on medium-high 4-5 minutes until the ham is hot (140°F).
Add the last oil, garlic and onion whites for 30 seconds, then the rice. Fry 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, butter, pepper, eggs and onion greens.

seasoning.base: garlic, soy sauce and black pepper
tryThis: a few drops of sesame oil
a pinch of red pepper flakes
seasoning.tip: Ham and soy sauce are salty; skip extra salt.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Chicken Thigh & Rice Pot
notes: Our take: Nature's Seasoning and fresh garlic instead of the oregano-thyme rub, chicken broth instead of vegetable, corn oil, and peas plus butter stirred in at the end.
steps: Rub the thighs with Nature's Seasoning, paprika, garlic powder and pepper.
Brown them in 1 Tbsp oil on medium, 3 minutes a side. Set aside (not cooked through yet).
Add the last oil and the onion; cook 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and rice for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and scrape the pan. Set the chicken on top, boil, then cover and cook on low 20 minutes.
Scatter the peas on top, lid back on, heat off, 5 minutes.
Check the chicken reads 165°F. Stir in the butter and serve.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic and paprika
tryThis: a squeeze of lemon at the end
seasoning.tip: Nature's Seasoning has salt in it, so don't add more.

title: WingsCrew Honey Garlic Mustard Sheet Pan
notes: Our take: no mayo (honey, mustard and melted butter instead), cheap russets and frozen green beans, yellow onion, Nature's Seasoning on the veggies, and the potatoes get a 15-minute head start.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with the oil and 1 tsp Nature's Seasoning on a sheet pan. Roast 15 minutes.
Stir the honey, mustards, butter, garlic and pepper together. Coat the chicken in half of it.
Stir the pan, add the frozen green beans and the last Nature's Seasoning, and lay the chicken on top.
Roast 20-25 minutes until the chicken reads 165°F. Brush on the rest of the sauce for the last 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: honey, mustard, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a pinch of smoked paprika in the sauce
seasoning.tip: Only the clean half of the sauce goes on at the end; keep it away from the raw chicken bowl.

title: WingsCrew Cracker-Crust Tuna Cakes
notes: Our take: crushed saltines instead of breadcrumbs, sharp cheddar and yellow mustard in the mix, Nature's Seasoning and garlic powder instead of seasoning salt and lemon, fried in corn oil.

ingredients.item: chunk light tuna in water, 5 oz each (Hill Country Fare), drained well

steps: Mix everything except the oil until it just holds together.
Shape 4 patties and chill 10 minutes so they hold.
Fry in the oil on medium 4-5 minutes a side, until golden and 160°F in the center.
Serve with hot sauce, in a tortilla or over lettuce.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder and mustard
tryThis: a dash of hot sauce in the mix
a squeeze of lemon at the table
seasoning.tip: Squeeze the tuna really dry or the cakes fall apart.

title: WingsCrew Ham, Potato & Cabbage Soup
notes: Our take: diced ham and potatoes make it a meal, chicken broth instead of vegetable, no green beans, bell pepper or parsley, Nature's Seasoning, and a shorter simmer.
steps: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil on medium 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, cabbage, tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth and spices.
Boil, then cover and simmer 25-30 minutes, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Stir in the ham and simmer 5 minutes, until it's hot (140°F). Taste for salt.
Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic, paprika and thyme
tryThis: a splash of vinegar at the end
seasoning.tip: Add the ham near the end and taste before salting; ham is salty.

title: WingsCrew Sheet Pan Thigh Fajitas
notes: Our take: juicy chicken thighs instead of breast, a hotter oven for less time, Nature's Seasoning instead of salt and sugar, corn tortillas and sharp cheddar.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in strips

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil and all the spices right on a sheet pan. Spread out.
Roast 20-25 minutes, stirring once, until the edges char and the chicken reads 165°F.
Squeeze the lime over the pan.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet and fill with fajitas, cheddar and sour cream.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, garlic, paprika and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Don't crowd the pan; use two pans if the veggies are piled up, or they steam.

title: WingsCrew Cast-Iron Fajita Meat
notes: Our take: plain fajita meat (skirt) instead of flank, a simple lime-garlic-cumin soak (no chipotle, coriander or Worcestershire), corn oil, Nature's Seasoning, peppers cooked in the steak pan, corn tortillas. Grill option: same temps over high heat.

ingredients.item: shredded sharp cheddar and sour cream (optional)

steps: Mix the lime juice, 1 Tbsp oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, Nature's Seasoning and honey in a bag. Add the meat.
Fridge 30 minutes to 8 hours.
Pat the meat dry. Sear in a smoking-hot cast-iron skillet 3-4 minutes a side, to 145°F. Rest 10 minutes.
Same pan, last oil: cook the peppers and onion 8-10 minutes, scraping up the brown bits.
Slice the meat thin across the grain, toss with the veggies and fill the tortillas.

seasoning.base: lime, garlic, cumin, chili powder and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a squeeze of fresh lime at the table
seasoning.tip: Pat the meat dry before it hits the pan so it browns instead of steaming.

title: WingsCrew Honey Cayenne Glazed Thighs
notes: Our take: a honey-garlic-butter glaze added at the end instead of a brown sugar rub (no burning), Nature's Seasoning instead of salt, a splash of hot sauce, corn oil.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and rub with Nature's Seasoning, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne and pepper.
Cook in the oil on medium, 5-6 minutes a side, until 165°F inside.
Turn to low. Add the butter and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the honey and hot sauce and turn the thighs 1-2 minutes, until sticky and glazed.

seasoning.base: honey, cayenne, paprika, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a squeeze of lime at the end
seasoning.tip: Add the honey only after the chicken is cooked; honey burns fast.

title: WingsCrew Chicken Thigh & Potato Stew
notes: Our take: cheap russets instead of baby potatoes, all chicken broth, Nature's Seasoning and thyme instead of four herbs, flour added once instead of twice, frozen peas at the end.
steps: Toss the chicken with Nature's Seasoning. Brown it in the butter and oil on medium, about 5 minutes. Set aside.
Cook the onion, celery and carrots 5 minutes. Add the garlic.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1-2 minutes.
Slowly stir in the broth, scraping the pot. Add the chicken, potatoes, thyme and pepper.
Boil, then simmer uncovered 25-30 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the chicken reads 165°F.
Stir in the peas for 3 minutes. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic, thyme and black pepper
tryThis: a bay leaf in the simmer
seasoning.tip: Taste at the end; potatoes soak up salt as they cook.

title: WingsCrew One-Skillet Ribeye & Garlic Potatoes
notes: Our take: russets with a microwave head start instead of boiled new potatoes, no radishes or red wine vinegar, garlic butter basting, Nature's Seasoning, peas straight from the freezer into the steak pan. Two 8 oz H-E-B Select value-pack ribeyes, sliced, feed 4.

ingredients.item: ribeye steaks, about 8 oz and ¾ inch thick each (H-E-B Select value pack)

steps: Season the steaks with Nature's Seasoning and pepper.
Microwave the potatoes with the water, covered, 5-6 minutes until nearly tender. Drain.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet on high. Sear the steaks 4-5 minutes a side.
Last minute: add 2 Tbsp butter and the garlic and spoon it over the steaks. Cook to 145°F, then rest 5 minutes.
Same pan, medium-high: fry the potatoes 6-8 minutes until crisp. Add the peas and last butter for 2 minutes.
Slice the steak and pour the juices over everything.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, black pepper and garlic butter
tryThis: a sprig of rosemary in the basting butter
a pinch of red pepper flakes on the potatoes
seasoning.tip: Nature's Seasoning is salty; don't add more salt to the potatoes until you taste.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Ribeye Rice Bowls
notes: Our take: no sake, mirin or dashi (a cheap soy-honey-garlic sauce instead), regular long-grain rice, spinach wilted in the same pan, no mayo rub, and an optional fried egg on top. About 12 oz of thin ribeye feeds 4.

ingredients.item: thin ribeye steaks, about ½ inch

steps: Cook the garlic in the oil on medium 3-4 minutes, until golden. Scoop it out.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan, 2 minutes, with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Turn the heat to high. Pepper the steaks and sear 2-3 minutes a side, to 145°F. Rest 5 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce, honey, water and cornstarch. Pour into the pan, bubble 1 minute, then stir in the butter and garlic.
Fill bowls with rice, sliced steak, spinach and sauce. Top with green onion and a fried egg (cook until the white is set).

seasoning.base: soy sauce, honey and fried garlic
tryThis: a few drops of sesame oil
seasoning.tip: Get the pan really hot so the thin steaks brown before they overcook.

title: WingsCrew Bacon, Egg & Potato Tacos
notes: Our take: Texas-style with diced potato fried in the bacon fat, eggs scrambled in the same pan, sharp cheddar, salsa instead of cherry tomatoes and avocado, and corn tortillas warmed in a little corn oil.
steps: Cook the bacon crisp, chop it, and keep 1 Tbsp fat in the pan.
Add the potato, cover, and cook on medium 8-10 minutes, stirring, until tender and browned.
Pour in the eggs with the garlic powder and pepper. Scramble until set with no runny egg.
Turn off the heat, stir in the bacon and top with cheddar.
Warm the tortillas in a skillet with a light film of corn oil. Fill and top with salsa.

seasoning.base: garlic powder, black pepper and bacon
seasoning.tip: Bacon brings the salt; taste before adding any.

title: WingsCrew Cowboy Breakfast Skillet
notes: Our take: cheap russets instead of Yukon or red potatoes, regular store-brand bacon, no mushrooms, Swiss chard or cilantro (green pepper, onion and optional spinach instead), Nature's Seasoning, sharp cheddar and eggs cooked firm.
steps: Cook the bacon in a big skillet until crisp. Crumble it; keep 2 tsp fat.
Add the potatoes for 2 minutes, then the water. Cover and steam 5 minutes.
Add the pepper, onion, garlic, Nature's Seasoning and black pepper. Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the bacon.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites and yolks are set, 6-8 minutes.
Top with cheddar and salsa.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic and black pepper
tryThis: a pinch of cumin on the potatoes
seasoning.tip: Bacon and Nature's Seasoning are both salty; no added salt needed.

title: J D's Ham Tacos
steps: Heat the ham until hot.
Lightly fry corn tortillas in corn oil.
While the tortillas and ham are still hot, add them together with the sharp cheese so the cheese melts.
Top with tomato slices and lettuce.
Salt the tomatoes when you plate.

seasoning.base: light salt on the tomatoes; the ham and sharp cheese carry the rest

title: J D's Microwave Baked Potatoes
steps: Poke holes all over the potatoes with a fork.
Microwave on high: 8 minutes for 1 potato, plus 1 minute for each extra potato (2 potatoes = 9 minutes, 3 = 10 minutes).
Remove the potatoes from the microwave. Careful, they're hot!
Put the potatoes on a plate and mash them flat with a fork, mixing in butter and cream cheese.
Season with garlic and a light sprinkle of salt.
Top with shredded sharp cheddar, then sprinkle Nature's Seasoning on top of the cheese.
Microwave until the cheese melts.
Cut a bite with your fork and eat. Enjoy!

seasoning.base: garlic, light salt and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a sprinkle of chives or green onion

title: WingsCrew Backyard Fajita Meat
notes: Our take: half the soy sauce (low-sodium) and honey instead of brown sugar, 3 limes instead of 6-8, a shorter 1-8 hour soak, cheaper green peppers grilled right on the grate (no skillet), corn tortillas charred on the grill. Works on gas or charcoal. Total includes 1 hour marinating.

ingredients.item: green bell peppers, halved and seeded
large yellow onion, cut in thick rounds
shredded sharp cheddar, salsa and sour cream (optional)

steps: Whisk the soy, lime, oil, honey, chili powder, cumin, garlic and pepper. Pour 3 Tbsp into a small bowl for the veggies.
Bag the meat with the rest. Fridge 1 to 8 hours.
Heat the grill to high. Brush the pepper halves and onion rounds with the saved marinade.
Wipe off the meat and grill 3-5 minutes a side, to 145°F. Rest 10 minutes.
Grill the veggies 8-10 minutes until charred. Char the tortillas 20 seconds a side.
Slice the meat and veggies thin and fill the tortillas.

seasoning.base: lime, garlic, chili powder, cumin and soy sauce
tryThis: a shake of Nature's Seasoning right off the grill
seasoning.tip: Lime breaks meat down; don't go past 8 hours or it turns mushy.

title: WingsCrew Nature's Seasoning Ribeyes with Garlic Butter
notes: Our take: Nature's Seasoning and garlic powder dry rub instead of plain kosher salt, cheaper 1-inch H-E-B Select value-pack ribeyes, a hot direct sear (cool side only if needed) instead of a slow reverse sear, and a garlic butter finish. Gas or charcoal. Total includes a 40-minute rest after seasoning.

ingredients.item: boneless ribeye steaks, about 1 inch thick (H-E-B Select value pack, 3-4 steaks)

steps: Rub the steaks with Nature's Seasoning, pepper and garlic powder. Fridge, uncovered, 40 minutes to overnight.
Mash the butter with the minced garlic.
Heat the grill to high with one cooler side.
Sear 3-4 minutes a side over the hot side. If the outside is done before 145°F, finish on the cool side, lid down.
At 145°F, rest 5 minutes with a spoon of garlic butter on each steak.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, black pepper and garlic
tryThis: a pinch of chili powder in the rub
a little honey in the garlic butter
seasoning.tip: Nature's Seasoning is the salt here; don't add more.

title: WingsCrew Honey Lime Garlic Thighs
notes: Our take: no soy, Worcestershire or Dijon (so it's gluten-free), Nature's Seasoning instead of kosher salt, chili powder instead of cayenne, corn oil, more honey, and a saved clean portion for basting. Marinate in the fridge only. Total includes a 30-minute marinade.
steps: Whisk everything except the chicken. Save 2 Tbsp in a cup for basting.
Coat the chicken with the rest and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes to 6 hours.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grate.
Grill 5-6 minutes a side, until 165°F. Brush with the saved sauce for the last minute.
Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: lime, garlic, honey, cumin and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: fajita seasoning instead of the cumin and chili powder
seasoning.tip: Honey can char; move the thighs to cooler grates if they darken too fast.

title: WingsCrew Fajita Foil Packs with Potatoes
notes: Our take: chicken thighs instead of breast, thin-sliced potatoes instead of zucchini, green peppers and yellow onion, Nature's Seasoning instead of kosher salt, a little corn oil, sharp cheddar melted in the packet, corn tortillas. Makes 6 packets.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs, ½-inch strips
medium russet potatoes, sliced ⅛ inch thick

steps: Heat the grill to about 450°F.
Microwave the potato slices, covered, 3 minutes so they finish on time.
Toss the chicken, potatoes, peppers and onion with the lime, oil and spices.
Divide onto 6 sprayed sheets of heavy foil and seal tight, leaving room for steam.
Grill 12-15 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F and the potatoes are tender.
Open carefully, add cheddar, close 1 minute to melt. Serve with tortillas.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: extra lime when you open the packets
seasoning.tip: Open one packet to check before pulling them all; thick strips take longer.

title: WingsCrew 5-5-5 Instant Pot Eggs
notes: Our take: the easy-to-remember 5-5-5 method (5 minutes high, 5 minutes natural release, 5 minutes ice bath) instead of 6-6-6, a trivet instead of a basket, and a Nature's Seasoning shake to eat them with. Total includes coming to pressure. For extra-firm yolks, cook 6 minutes.

ingredients.item: large eggs, cold from the fridge (Great Value)
Nature's Seasoning and black pepper, for sprinkling

steps: Set the trivet in the pot, add the water, and stand the eggs on it.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 5 minutes.
Let it release on its own 5 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Move the eggs to ice water for 5 minutes.
Peel under running water. Yolks should be fully set. Sprinkle with Nature's Seasoning and pepper.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Peel from the fat end where the air pocket is; it comes off easier.

title: WingsCrew Ham & Cheddar Cream Cheese Egg Bites
notes: Our take: cream cheese blended in instead of most of the milk for a velvety bite, more sharp cheddar, ham only, Nature's Seasoning and garlic powder instead of salt, foil over the trays, and a longer natural release so the centers set. Makes 14. Needs two silicone egg-bite trays, a trivet and a sling. Total includes coming to pressure.
steps: Blend or hard-whisk the eggs, cream cheese, milk and seasonings until smooth.
Grease two silicone trays. Add ham, cheddar and green onion to each cup, then fill ⅔ with egg.
Cover each tray loosely with foil and stack them on the trivet with a sling. Add 1 cup water to the pot.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 10 minutes. Natural release 10 minutes, then vent.
Check the centers are firm with no liquid egg. Cool 5 minutes and pop out. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder and black pepper
tryThis: a spoon of salsa on top
diced green chiles in the cups
seasoning.tip: Ham and cheddar are salty; don't add extra salt.

title: WingsCrew Ham, Potato & 15 Bean Soup
notes: Our take: no ham bone, more diced ham added for the second cook instead, Ro-Tel instead of crushed tomatoes, a diced potato and black pepper instead of spinach and lemon, and a slightly longer second cook for tender beans and potatoes. Total includes the 1-hour soak inside the pot.

ingredients.item: Hurst's HamBeens 15 Bean Soup with seasoning packet, 20 oz (Walmart)

steps: Set the seasoning packet aside. Rinse the beans and pick out any stones.
On Sauté, cook the onion and carrots in the oil 3 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans and water. Seal, High Pressure 1 minute, then let it sit sealed 1 hour to soak.
Release any pressure. Stir in the Ro-Tel, potato, ham, chili powder, pepper and the packet.
Seal, High Pressure 5 minutes. Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Check the beans are tender (if not, 3 more minutes at High). The ham is now well past 140°F. Salt to taste. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: the ham seasoning packet, garlic, onion, chili powder and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Add salt only at the end; the packet and ham are already salty.

title: WingsCrew Bacon & Jalapeño Instant Pot Black Beans
notes: Our take: bacon rendered first for flavor, jalapeño instead of bell pepper, chili powder instead of oregano and bay leaves, a cup more water so they stay saucy, salt at the end, lime to finish. Same 35-minute cook and 20-minute natural release. No soaking.
steps: Pick through the beans for stones.
On Sauté, cook the bacon 4-5 minutes until crisp. Add the onion and jalapeño for 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the water and beans, scraping the bottom. Seal and cook on High Pressure 35 minutes.
Natural release 20 minutes. Stir in salt to taste and a squeeze of lime.

seasoning.base: bacon, garlic, cumin, chili powder and lime
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning instead of the salt
seasoning.tip: Salt at the end so you don't over-salt; the bacon adds some.

title: WingsCrew Honey Peanut Butter Chicken (Instant Pot)
notes: Our take: no browning step (dump and go), honey and fresh garlic added, no cilantro or ground ginger, more peanut butter set on top instead of stirred in so it won't scorch, and a short natural release. Written for a 6-quart pot.
steps: Pour the broth, soy sauce and lime juice into the pot.
Add the chicken. Scatter the garlic and pepper flakes on top, then spoon on the peanut butter and honey. Don't stir.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 9 minutes. Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Lift out the chicken and check it reads 165°F.
On Sauté, stir the cornstarch and water into the sauce and simmer until thick. Return the chicken and coat.
Serve over rice with green onions.

seasoning.base: peanut butter, honey, garlic, soy sauce and lime
tryThis: a little hot sauce in the sauce
seasoning.tip: Keep the peanut butter on top until after cooking; stirred in at the start it can trigger a burn warning.

title: WingsCrew Honey Cinnamon Banana Muffins
notes: Our take: honey instead of maple syrup, melted butter instead of canola oil, regular all-purpose flour instead of white whole wheat, walnut chips cut in half, and a cinnamon-sugar top. The flour, baking soda, egg and fat amounts stay the same so they still rise right. Makes 12.

ingredients.item: sugar mixed with ¼ tsp cinnamon, for the tops

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line or grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mash the bananas. Whisk in the egg, yogurt and butter, then the brown sugar, honey and vanilla.
Stir in the baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
Fold in the flour until just mixed, then the walnuts.
Fill the cups, sprinkle with cinnamon sugar, and bake 20-22 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, honey, vanilla and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a few chocolate chips instead of walnuts
seasoning.tip: Stop stirring once the flour disappears; overmixing makes tough muffins.

title: WingsCrew Ham, Bacon & Sharp Cheddar Quiche
notes: Our take: a store-brand frozen crust (no rolling), sharp cheddar instead of Gruyère, crumbled bacon added, garlic powder and Nature's Seasoning instead of nutmeg and most of the salt, yellow mustard. The egg-to-milk ratio stays the same so it sets right.

ingredients.item: frozen 9-inch pie crust (Great Value), thawed 10 minutes

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Prick the crust, line with foil and dried beans, bake 10 minutes. Remove foil, bake 3 more. Lower to 350°F.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and seasonings.
Scatter the ham, bacon, cheddar and green onion in the crust. Pour in the eggs.
Bake on a sheet pan 40-50 minutes, until the center is set and reads 160°F. Foil the edge if it browns fast.
Rest 10 minutes and slice.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder and black pepper
tryThis: a pinch of nutmeg if you miss it
seasoning.tip: Ham, bacon and cheddar bring plenty of salt; don't add more.

title: WingsCrew Chocolate Chip Peanut Oat Cookies
notes: Our take: old-fashioned oats instead of quick oats (chewier, one cheap bag), all-purpose flour instead of white whole wheat, and the mix-ins changed to chocolate chips and chopped peanuts (no raisins or walnuts). Butter, egg, honey, applesauce and baking powder stay the same so the dough behaves. Makes 24. Total includes 30 minutes chilling. Don't eat raw dough.
steps: Whisk the oats, flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl whisk the applesauce, butter, egg, vanilla and honey.
Stir wet into dry just until mixed. Fold in the chips and peanuts.
Chill at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Drop 1½-inch balls on a lined sheet and flatten a little.
Bake 9-11 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool 2 minutes on the pan.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, vanilla, honey and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a drizzle of peanut butter on warm cookies
seasoning.tip: Chill the dough; it's sticky and spreads if baked warm.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Butter Thighs & Potatoes Sheet Pan
notes: Our take: potatoes roast alongside so it's a full meal on one pan, Nature's Seasoning and garlic butter instead of Italian seasoning and lemon, corn oil, and no marinating wait.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes and onion with the oil and 1 tsp Nature's Seasoning on a sheet pan.
Pat the thighs dry, rub with paprika, pepper and the last Nature's Seasoning, and set them skin-up on the veggies.
Bake 25 minutes. Mix the butter and garlic and brush it on the skin. Stir the potatoes.
Bake 15-20 minutes more, until the thighs read 165°F near the bone and the potatoes are tender. Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, paprika, garlic butter and black pepper
tryThis: a pinch of cayenne in the rub
seasoning.tip: Pat the skin really dry so it crisps.

title: WingsCrew Ham & Cheese Egg Rice Skillet
notes: Our take: diced ham and garlic for protein and flavor, hot sauce instead of gochujang, butter and corn oil instead of sesame oil, less soy sauce (low-sodium), sharp cheddar on top. Day-old rice warmed in the pan works best.
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a big nonstick skillet on medium. Cook the ham and garlic 2-3 minutes until the ham is hot (140°F).
Add the rice and stir 2 minutes to warm it.
Push it to one side. Scramble the eggs in the empty side until fully set, then fold together.
Stir in the soy sauce and hot sauce. Top with cheddar and green onions.

seasoning.base: garlic, soy sauce and hot sauce
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning instead of the soy sauce
a few drops of sesame oil
seasoning.tip: Ham, soy and cheddar are all salty; skip added salt.

title: WingsCrew Crispy Corn Tortilla Bean Quesadillas & Ro-Tel Rice
notes: Our take: corn tortillas crisped in corn oil instead of flour tortillas, mashed pinto beans with cumin, garlic and Nature's Seasoning instead of Bayou Blend, sharp cheddar, and rice made from scratch with Ro-Tel instead of a packet (cheaper and gluten-free). Serving = 2 quesadillas + about ¾ cup rice.

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes & green chiles, 10 oz (H-E-B), with juice
frozen fajita vegetable blend, thawed and chopped (optional)

steps: Toast the rice in 1 Tbsp oil 2 minutes. Add the Ro-Tel, water and Nature's Seasoning. Boil, cover, and cook on low 18 minutes. Rest 5.
Mash the beans with the veggies, cumin, garlic powder and Nature's Seasoning.
Spread beans on 8 tortillas, top with cheddar and another tortilla.
Fry in a thin film of corn oil on medium 2-3 minutes a side, until crisp and melty.
Cut and serve with the rice.

seasoning.base: cumin, garlic, Nature's Seasoning and Ro-Tel
seasoning.tip: Mash the beans well so they glue the corn tortillas together.

title: WingsCrew Bacon & Egg Freezer Quesadillas
notes: Our take: bacon instead of white beans, eggs scrambled in the bacon fat, sharp cheddar, store-brand fajita-size flour tortillas instead of whole wheat, Nature's Seasoning instead of kosher salt, spinach optional. Makes 8. Freeze up to 2 months; microwave 2-3 minutes from frozen to 165°F.
steps: Cook the bacon crisp and crumble it. Keep 1 Tbsp fat in the pan.
Whisk the eggs, milk and seasonings.
Wilt the spinach in the fat 1 minute, then add the eggs. Scramble on medium-low until just set, about 5 minutes. Stir in the bacon.
Fill each tortilla with cheddar and egg and fold in half.
Wipe the pan and cook the quesadillas on medium 2-3 minutes a side until golden.
To freeze, cool first, wrap each one and freeze flat.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Bacon and Nature's Seasoning bring the salt; don't add more.

title: WingsCrew Sausage & Cabbage Egg Roll Skillet
notes: Our take: cheaper pork breakfast sausage instead of ground turkey, a half head of green cabbage instead of bagged broccoli slaw, no mushrooms, ground ginger, hot sauce instead of sambal, and a touch of honey instead of rice vinegar and sesame oil.

ingredients.item: pork breakfast sausage roll (Great Value Original)
head green cabbage, thinly sliced (about 6 cups)

steps: Brown the sausage in a big skillet on medium-high, breaking it up, 6-8 minutes, until no pink and 160°F.
Add the cabbage and carrots and cook 5-6 minutes until wilted.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce, honey, hot sauce and pepper. Toss 1 minute and top with green onions.

seasoning.base: garlic, ginger, soy sauce and hot sauce
tryThis: a few drops of sesame oil
seasoning.tip: Sausage is already seasoned; taste before adding more soy.

title: WingsCrew Sausage Gravy & Garlic Cheddar Biscuit Skillet
notes: Our take: store-brand sausage and butter, Nature's Seasoning and garlic powder in the gravy with less added salt, garlic powder instead of parsley in the biscuits, more sharp cheddar, and garlic butter brushed on top. The biscuit flour, baking powder, butter and milk amounts are unchanged so they still rise. One oven-safe skillet.

ingredients.item: salted butter (for gravy, Hill Country Fare)
salted butter, melted, mixed with 1 minced garlic clove

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Brown the sausage in an oven-safe skillet until no pink and 160°F.
Stir in 2 Tbsp butter, then ¼ cup flour. Cook 1 minute.
Slowly stir in 3 cups milk, pepper, Nature's Seasoning and garlic powder. Cook 3-5 minutes until thick. Heat off.
Whisk the biscuit flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and garlic powder. Cut in the cold butter until crumbly.
Stir in the milk and cheddar just until a thick dough forms.
Drop 10 spoonfuls on the hot gravy, brush with garlic butter, and bake 25-28 minutes until golden and cooked through (no raw dough in the middle). Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: black pepper, Nature's Seasoning and garlic
tryThis: red pepper flakes in the gravy
seasoning.tip: Taste the gravy before the biscuits go on; sausage salt varies by brand.

title: WingsCrew Cheesy Ham Scalloped Potatoes
notes: Our take: cheap russets instead of Yukon Gold, diced ham and sharp cheddar layered in (more like au gratin), fresh garlic and Nature's Seasoning instead of onion powder, nutmeg and cayenne, and less salt in the boiling water. The butter-flour-milk sauce ratio is the same. A meal with a salad, or a side for steak.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9×9 dish. Peel and slice the potatoes ¼ inch. Boil 5 minutes in salted water; drain.
Warm the milk and broth together.
Melt the butter with the garlic, stir in the flour until bubbly, then whisk in the warm milk. Simmer until thick.
Off the heat, stir in Nature's Seasoning, pepper and 1 cup cheddar.
Layer half the potatoes, all the ham and half the sauce. Repeat with potatoes and sauce. Top with the last cheddar.
Bake covered 30 minutes, then uncovered 30 minutes until golden and tender. Rest 15 minutes. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: garlic, Nature's Seasoning and black pepper
tryThis: a pinch of dry mustard in the sauce
seasoning.tip: Ham, cheddar and salted butter all add salt; taste the sauce before adding any.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Butter Hasselbacks
notes: Our take: melted butter and corn oil with fresh garlic instead of plain vegetable oil and garlic powder, Nature's Seasoning instead of kosher salt, and sharp cheddar and bacon bits melted on for the last 5 minutes. One potato each.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan. Scrub and dry the potatoes.
Set each potato between two chopsticks and slice thin, ⅛-¼ inch, stopping at the sticks.
Mix the butter, oil, garlic, Nature's Seasoning and pepper. Brush half over the potatoes.
Bake 35 minutes. Brush the rest between the slices and bake 30 minutes more, until tender in the middle.
Top with cheddar and bacon and bake 5 minutes to melt.

seasoning.base: garlic butter, Nature's Seasoning and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Fan the slices open a little at the halfway brush so the butter gets inside.

title: WingsCrew Cream Cheese Garlic Mashers (Instant Pot)
notes: Our take: steamed in a basket over 1½ cups water (comes to pressure much faster than covering in 6 cups, so less waiting), whole garlic cloves cooked with the potatoes, cream cheese with less butter, Nature's Seasoning, and optional sharp cheddar, J D style. Serving is 1 cup.
steps: Pour the water in the pot, add a steamer basket, and pile in the potatoes and garlic.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 8 minutes. Quick release.
Lift out the basket and pour off the water.
Put the potatoes and garlic back in the pot. Mash with the butter, cream cheese, Nature's Seasoning and pepper.
Add the warm milk a little at a time and stir in the cheddar. Don't over-mash or they get gummy.

seasoning.base: garlic, Nature's Seasoning, butter and cream cheese
seasoning.tip: Nature's Seasoning brings the salt; taste before adding plain salt.

title: WingsCrew Nature's Seasoning Butter Corn
notes: Our take: husks off and grilled bare for real char (no soaking), brushed with corn oil, then rolled in a garlic, Nature's Seasoning and chili-lime butter instead of plain butter and sea salt.
steps: Heat the grill to medium-high.
Brush the corn with the oil.
Grill 10-12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred in spots.
Mash the butter with the garlic, Nature's Seasoning and chili powder.
Roll the hot corn in the butter and squeeze on the lime.

seasoning.base: garlic butter, Nature's Seasoning and chili-lime
tryThis: shredded sharp cheddar on the hot corn
seasoning.tip: Turn the corn often; bare kernels go from charred to burnt fast.

title: WingsCrew Honey Dijon Garlic Grilled Thighs
notes: Our take: honey instead of brown sugar, lemon juice instead of balsamic, Nature's Seasoning instead of lemon pepper, four garlic cloves instead of one, corn oil, no soy sauce (so it's gluten-free), and a clean saved portion for basting. Total includes at least 30 minutes marinating (up to 4 hours).
steps: Whisk everything except the chicken. Save 2 Tbsp in a cup for basting.
Coat the thighs with the rest and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes to 4 hours.
Grill on medium-high 5-7 minutes a side, until 165°F.
Brush with the saved sauce at the end. Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: honey, Dijon, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a pinch of red pepper flakes
fajita seasoning for a Tex-Mex take
seasoning.tip: Keep the saved basting sauce away from the raw chicken.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Steak Soak
notes: Our take: written as a full recipe with 2 lb of ribeye or fajita meat; less than half the oil, soy and Worcestershire; lime instead of lemon; black pepper instead of white; fresh garlic instead of dried minced; far less basil; a spoon of honey; whisked by hand instead of blended. Total includes 1 hour marinating (up to 8).

ingredients.item: ribeye steaks (H-E-B Select value pack) or fajita meat

steps: Whisk everything except the steak in a bowl.
Bag the steak with the marinade. Fridge 1 to 8 hours.
Heat the grill to high. Lift the steak out, pat dry, and throw out the used marinade.
Grill 3-5 minutes a side, to 145°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice.

seasoning.base: garlic, soy sauce, Worcestershire, lime and black pepper
tryThis: a shake of Nature's Seasoning right off the grill (go light)
a pinch of red pepper flakes
seasoning.tip: Soy is salty; skip extra salt and pat the steak dry for a better crust.

title: WingsCrew Honey Chili Fajita Thighs
notes: Our take: boneless thighs grilled whole and then sliced (instead of breast strips that fall through the grate), half the oil (corn oil), less garlic powder plus fresh garlic, cumin and Nature's Seasoning added (so it isn't bland), a shorter 2-hour marinade, and corn tortillas. Total includes 2 hours marinating (up to overnight).

ingredients.item: grilled onions and peppers, salsa and shredded sharp cheddar (optional)

steps: Whisk everything except the chicken and tortillas.
Bag the thighs with the marinade. Fridge 2 hours to overnight.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grate. Throw out the used marinade.
Grill the thighs 6-7 minutes a side, until 165°F. Rest 5 minutes.
Slice into strips and serve in warm corn tortillas.

seasoning.base: chili powder, garlic, lime, honey, cumin and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Slice after resting so the juices stay in the meat.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Herb Grilled Thighs
notes: Our take: boneless thighs instead of thin breasts, cheaper apple cider vinegar instead of red wine vinegar, no soy sauce (Nature's Seasoning instead, so it's gluten-free), fresh garlic plus more garlic powder, corn oil and a spoon of honey, grilled on medium. Total includes 1 hour marinating (up to 4).
steps: Whisk everything except the chicken.
Bag the chicken with the marinade. Fridge 1 to 4 hours.
Heat the grill to medium and oil the grate. Throw out the used marinade.
Grill 6-7 minutes a side, until 165°F. Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: garlic, oregano, parsley, basil and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a squeeze of lemon after grilling
seasoning.tip: Vinegar works fast; 4 hours is the max or the texture gets mushy.

title: WingsCrew Ro-Tel Salsa Chicken Thighs (Instant Pot)
notes: Our take: thawed boneless thighs instead of frozen breasts, a homemade chili-cumin-garlic rub instead of a taco packet (cheaper, and no wheat worries), Ro-Tel added to the salsa, twice the batch, and sharp cheddar stirred in. Total includes coming to pressure and a 10-minute natural release. Use it in corn tortillas, bowls or on a baked potato.

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes & green chiles, 10 oz (H-E-B), with juice

steps: Pour the broth into the pot.
Rub the thighs with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and Nature's Seasoning and lay them in.
Pour the Ro-Tel and salsa on top. Don't stir.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 10 minutes. Natural release 10 minutes, then vent.
Check the chicken reads 165°F. Shred it in the sauce and stir in the cheddar.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, garlic, Nature's Seasoning and salsa
tryThis: a squeeze of lime after shredding
seasoning.tip: Broth goes in first and salsa on top so the bottom doesn't scorch.

title: WingsCrew Tomato Butter Chicken & Potatoes (Instant Pot)
notes: Our take: a cheap pantry spice mix (curry powder, cumin, paprika) instead of six spices with garam masala and cardamom, potatoes instead of cauliflower, butter instead of ghee, cream cheese instead of coconut milk, and one pressure cook instead of two. Tomatoes aren't drained and broth goes in so the pot has enough thin liquid. Serve over rice or as is.

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes, 14.5 oz (Great Value), with juice

steps: On Sauté, melt 1 Tbsp butter and cook the onion 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and scrape the bottom clean.
Add the chicken and potatoes. Pour the tomatoes on top; don't stir.
Seal and cook on High Pressure 8 minutes. Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Check the chicken reads 165°F and the potatoes are tender.
On Sauté, stir in the peas, cream cheese and last butter for 2 minutes, until creamy.

seasoning.base: curry powder, cumin, paprika, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a squeeze of lime at the end
a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp
seasoning.tip: Scrape the bottom well after the spices so the pot doesn't throw a burn warning.

title: WingsCrew Cream Cheese Chicken Thigh Chili (Instant Pot)
notes: Our take: thighs instead of breasts, garlic, Nature's Seasoning and oregano instead of a ranch packet, cheaper pinto beans instead of white beans, frozen corn plus extra broth instead of canned corn with juice, and sharp cheddar on top. 1-cup servings. Good over a baked potato.

ingredients.item: black beans, drained and rinsed (15 oz)
diced tomatoes & green chiles, 10 oz (H-E-B), with juice
cream cheese, cut in 6 pieces (Great Value)
tortilla chips or baked potatoes, to serve

steps: Pour the broth in the pot. Add the chicken, beans, onion, corn, Ro-Tel and garlic.
Sprinkle in the spices and nudge some liquid under the chicken.
Set the cream cheese on top. Seal and cook on High Pressure 15 minutes. Natural release 10 minutes, then vent.
Check the chicken reads 165°F. Shred it and stir the cream cheese through.
Serve topped with cheddar. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic, oregano and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Ro-Tel and Nature's Seasoning are salty; taste before adding salt.

title: WingsCrew Cream Cheese Twice-Baked Spuds
notes: Our take: microwave the first bake (like J D's microwave potatoes) instead of an hour in the oven, cream cheese instead of sour cream, fresh garlic, a little less butter, green onions instead of chives, and Nature's Seasoning on top of the cheese. 12 halves from 6 small russets; make ahead and bake when needed.
steps: Poke the potatoes with a fork. Microwave 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until fork-tender. Cool 5 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Halve the potatoes and scoop out the insides, leaving a thin shell.
Mash the insides with the cream cheese, butter, garlic, salt and pepper. Add milk only if dry.
Fold in the bacon, green onions and half the cheddar.
Fill the shells, top with the rest of the cheddar and a sprinkle of Nature's Seasoning.
Bake 15 minutes until hot and melty (20-25 minutes, to 165°F, if made ahead and chilled).

seasoning.base: garlic, cream cheese, Nature's Seasoning and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Bacon, cheddar and Nature's Seasoning are salty; go light on the salt in the mash.

title: WingsCrew Hot-Oven Crispy Thighs
notes: Our take: a hotter 425°F oven for about 45 minutes instead of 350°F for an hour, the thighs on a rack, a pinch of baking powder in the rub for crackly skin, and Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder, paprika and pepper instead of garlic salt, onion salt, oregano and thyme. Bone-in, skin-on.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with foil, set a rack on it and spray it.
Pat the thighs very dry.
Mix the seasonings and baking powder and rub them all over, mostly on the skin.
Bake skin-up 40-50 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the thighs read 165°F near the bone.
Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, garlic powder, paprika and black pepper
tryThis: a drizzle of honey and hot sauce at the end
seasoning.tip: Use baking powder, not baking soda, and keep it to a light dusting or it tastes bitter.

title: WingsCrew Garlic Butter Fajita Fried Rice
notes: Our take: made for leftover fajita meat or chicken thighs, butter for most of the fat instead of ¼ cup olive oil, a third egg, frozen peas and carrots added, low-sodium soy, more rice. Done in 20 minutes.

ingredients.item: chopped leftover fajita meat or chicken thighs

steps: Heat the oil and 1 Tbsp butter in a big skillet on medium-high. Scramble the eggs until set; move to a plate.
Add 1 Tbsp butter, the meat, peas and carrots, garlic and green onion. Stir 3 minutes, until the meat is hot (165°F).
Add the rice and fry 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, pepper, eggs and last butter. Toss 1 minute.

seasoning.base: garlic butter, soy sauce and green onion
tryThis: a few drops of sesame oil
Nature's Seasoning instead of some of the soy
seasoning.tip: Cold leftover rice fries; fresh warm rice turns mushy.

title: WingsCrew Sausage, Potato & Egg Freezer Burritos
notes: Our take: diced potatoes stretch the filling, a homemade chili-cumin-garlic mix instead of a taco packet, no canned jalapeños, tomato or cilantro (they make burritos soggy; add salsa when you eat), store-brand sausage and fajita-size flour tortillas, sharp cheddar. Makes 16; microwave one 2-3 minutes from frozen.
steps: Brown the sausage and onion in a big skillet until no pink and 160°F. Scoop into a bowl.
Add the oil and potatoes. Cover and cook 10 minutes, then uncover and crisp 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and spices. Add to the bowl.
Whisk the eggs and milk and scramble in the butter until set. Add to the bowl.
Mix and cool 15 minutes, then stir in the cheddar.
Fill and roll the tortillas tight. Wrap each and freeze.
Reheat from frozen 2-3 minutes, until 165°F in the center.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, garlic and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: salsa or Ro-Tel on the side
seasoning.tip: Cool the filling before rolling so the tortillas don't get soggy.

title: WingsCrew Garlic-Lime Skillet Thigh Fajitas
notes: Our take: boneless thighs instead of breast cutlets, corn oil instead of olive oil, fresh garlic and Nature's Seasoning instead of onion powder and sea salt, veggies first then chicken in the same hot pan, and corn tortillas with sharp cheddar and sour cream.

ingredients.item: sour cream and salsa, to serve

steps: Stir 1 Tbsp oil, the lime juice, garlic and spices in a bowl. Coat the thighs (up to 4 hours ahead, in the fridge).
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a cast-iron skillet on medium-high. Cook the peppers and onion 5-6 minutes until charred in spots. Move to a plate.
Add the last oil and the thighs. Cook 5-6 minutes a side, until 165°F. Rest 5 minutes.
Slice the chicken, toss it back in with the veggies, and serve in tortillas with cheddar, sour cream and salsa.

seasoning.base: garlic, lime, chili powder, cumin, paprika and Nature's Seasoning
seasoning.tip: Cook the veggies first in the clean hot pan; then the chicken picks up their brown bits.

title: WingsCrew Bacon Cheddar Egg Salad
notes: Our take: crumbled bacon and sharp cheddar added, green onion instead of dill, chives and red onion (cheaper), part cream cheese instead of all mayo, yellow mustard instead of Dijon, and Nature's Seasoning instead of salt. Use the WingsCrew 5-5-5 Instant Pot Eggs. Keep cold; eat within 3-4 days.
steps: Stir the mayo, cream cheese, mustard, lemon juice, Nature's Seasoning and pepper until smooth.
Add the eggs, bacon, cheddar, green onions and celery and fold together.
Taste, sprinkle with paprika, and chill or eat right away.
Great on toast, in a tortilla or with crackers.

seasoning.base: Nature's Seasoning, yellow mustard, paprika and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Bacon, cheddar and Nature's Seasoning are all salty; taste before adding more.

title: WingsCrew Peanut Butter Center Chocolate Mug Cake
notes: Our take: melted butter instead of canola oil, a spoon of peanut butter sunk in the middle, a pinch of cinnamon, and all milk instead of milk plus water. Flour, sugar, cocoa and baking soda stay the same so it still rises. Microwaves vary; start checking at 1½ minutes. Don't eat it raw.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, salt and cinnamon in a big mug.
Stir in the milk, butter and vanilla until smooth.
Drop the peanut butter in the middle and push it just under the batter.
Microwave about 1 minute 45 seconds, until the top is set and springs back.
Cool 1 minute and eat from the mug.

seasoning.base: cocoa, vanilla, cinnamon and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a few chocolate chips on top
seasoning.tip: The peanut butter center stays molten and hot; let it sit a minute.

title: WingsCrew Peanut Butter Honey Crispy Bars
notes: Our take: store-brand cereal and marshmallows, ½ cup peanut butter melted in, salted butter cut to 6 Tbsp (the peanut butter adds richness) with no extra salt, a spoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon. No-bake. Allow about 1 more hour to cool before cutting. Keeps 3 days covered at room temperature.

ingredients.item: salted butter (Hill Country Fare), plus more for the pan
mini marshmallows (Great Value), divided (6 cups + 2 cups)

steps: Grease a 9×9 pan with a little butter, then lay in parchment.
Melt the butter in a big pot on medium-low. Add 6 cups marshmallows and stir just until melted.
Off the heat, stir in the peanut butter, honey, vanilla and cinnamon until smooth.
Stir in the cereal, then fold in the last 2 cups marshmallows.
Press lightly into the pan. Cool 1 hour, then cut.

seasoning.base: peanut butter, honey, vanilla and a pinch of cinnamon
tryThis: a drizzle of chocolate syrup on top
seasoning.tip: Keep the heat low; overcooked marshmallows make hard bars.

title: WingsCrew Honey Cinnamon Peanut Butter Cookies
notes: Our take: a half batch (2 dozen, every amount cut exactly in half), creamy store-brand peanut butter instead of crunchy, salted butter with less added salt, cinnamon in the dough, and a honey drizzle on the warm cookies. Butter, sugar, egg, flour and leavening ratios are unchanged. Total includes 1 hour chilling. Don't eat the raw dough (raw egg and flour).
steps: Beat the butter, peanut butter and both sugars until smooth. Beat in the egg.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon just until mixed. Chill 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Roll 1-inch balls, set 2 inches apart, and press a crisscross with a fork.
Bake 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden. Cool 2 minutes on the pan.
Drizzle the warm cookies with honey.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, honey and a little salt
tryThis: a sprinkle of flaky salt before baking
a few chocolate chips pressed on top
seasoning.tip: Chill the full hour so the cookies don't spread flat.

title: J D's Banana Peanut Butter Scoop
steps: Peel the banana and split it lengthwise down the middle, like a banana split, and lay the halves in a bowl or on a plate.
Add a scoop of peanut butter on top.
Drizzle a generous amount of honey on top.
Add a lighter drizzle of chocolate syrup, less than the honey.
Sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Enjoy!

seasoning.base: a sprinkle of cinnamon
tryThis: a pinch of salt on the peanut butter

title: Dove Slush

ingredients.item: Welch's Cran-Grape juice, or Welch's grape juice

steps: Fill the blender with ice.
Add one frozen container of grape juice concentrate (Welch's is best).
Add 1 cup of Welch's Cran-Grape, or just Welch's grape juice.
Blend until smooth, but not watery.
Layer the slush in a cup with vanilla ice cream.
notes: Makes 3 to 4 cups, maybe more depending on your glass. Watch out for the brain freeze! J D prefers Welch's.

seasoning.base: none needed
